t.1.200.1: Janamejaya said: Having thus obtained that kingdom in Indraprastha, O ascetic rich in austerity, what did the great-souled Pāṇḍavas do after that?
t.1.200.2: All my forefathers of old were great-souled men indeed; and how did Draupadī, their lawful wife, conduct herself toward them?
t.1.200.3: Or how did those five illustrious lords of men, all devoted to the one Kṛṣṇā, not become divided against one another?
t.1.200.4: O you whose wealth is austerity, I wish to hear in full detail everything about their conduct toward one another, joined as they were with that Kṛṣṇā.
t.1.200.5: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With Dhṛtarāṣṭra's leave, the Pāṇḍavas, tigers among men and scorchers of their foes, having obtained their kingdom, took their delight together with Kṛṣṇā.
t.1.200.6: Having obtained the kingdom, the greatly splendid Yudhiṣṭhira, true to his word, ruled the earth righteously together with his brothers.
t.1.200.7: Having conquered their enemies, the greatly wise sons of Pāṇḍu, wholly devoted to truth and dharma, attained the highest joy and dwelt there.
t.1.200.8: Performing all the affairs of the citizens, those bulls among men sat upon costly royal seats.
t.1.200.9: Then, when all those great-souled ones were seated, Nārada, the divine seer, arrived by chance. Yudhiṣṭhira gave him his own splendid seat.
t.1.200.10: When the divine seer had taken his seat, wise Yudhiṣṭhira himself offered him the guest-water according to the rite, and he made over the kingdom to him.
t.1.200.11: Having accepted that homage, the seer became glad at heart; and having honored him with blessings, he said to him, "Let it be sat," bidding him be seated.
t.1.200.13: And Draupadī too, as soon as she heard, became pure and composed, and went to where Nārada was seated with the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.200.12: Given leave, King Yudhiṣṭhira then sat down, and he sent word to Kṛṣṇā that the blessed lord had arrived.
t.1.200.14: Then the daughter of Drupada, who walked in dharma, saluted the feet of that divine seer and stood with joined palms, her body well covered.
t.1.200.15: And that righteous-souled, truthful Nārada, best of seers, having pronounced various blessings upon the princess, the blessed one said to that blameless lady, "You may go."
t.1.200.16: Then, when Kṛṣṇā had gone, the blessed seer spoke in private to all the Pāṇḍavas, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head.
t.1.200.17: Pāñcālī, the glorious one, is the one lawful wife of you all; so let a policy be adopted that no division may arise among you over this.
t.1.200.18: There were two Asura brothers, Sunda and Upasunda, ever united, who could not be slain by others and were renowned throughout the three worlds.
t.1.200.19: Those two, who had shared one kingdom, one house, one bed, one seat and one meal, struck each other down for the sake of Tilottamā.
t.1.200.20: Therefore let your friendship, founded on mutual regard, be guarded; do that, Yudhiṣṭhira, by which there may be no division among you in this matter.
t.1.200.21: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O great sage, whose sons were the two asuras Sunda and Upasunda? How did the rift between them arise, and how did they kill each other?
t.1.200.23: All this, just as it happened, we wish to hear in full, O Brahmin rich in austerities, for great is our curiosity.
t.1.200.22: Was this Tilottamā an apsaras or a daughter of the gods, and whose was she, maddened by desire for whom those two struck each other down?
